notes.decision: ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲭⲧⲟ analyzed as Lyc. action-noun ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ, ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ†ⲟⲩⲱ in glossary) on ⲭⲧⲟ = ϫⲡⲟ 'beget.' The chapter title is thus 'the begetting of Adam.' Distinguished from homophonous ⲕⲧⲟ 'turn.'

Three distinct verbs of fashioning preserved: ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲥⲉ 'mold' (πλάσσω, archonic fashioning), ϩⲱⲅⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'depict/paint' (ζωγραφέω, image-painting), ⲭⲡⲟ 'beget' (ϫⲡⲟ, generative birth). The catechumen's question parses Adam's origin into these three registers.

Parsed as relative perfect ⲛ̄ⲧⲁ-ⲛ-(ⲧ)ⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ-ⲩ 'whom we have likened (to him)' — i.e., 'those to whom we (might) compare him.' The sense is that Adam stands incomparable to anyone we could put alongside him in strength.

Tentatively parsed as Lyc. emphatic-reflexive ϩⲱⲟⲩ-ⲁⲛⲟⲩ 'they themselves' (cognate with Sah. ϩⲱⲟⲩ + intensive). Reading: Adam's contemporaries 'themselves were likewise in their years' — i.e., they too lived long lives, in contrast with today's diminished men.

Translated as 'abundant' tentatively. The form is opaque; it modifies ⲥⲟⲫⲓⲁ in apposition to ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲙⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'prudence-of-mind' (line 6). May be related to a root meaning depth/fullness/extension. Could alternatively read 'deep' or 'unfailing.' No exact parallel located in this corpus.

Parsed ⲛⲧⲁⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ as ⲛⲧⲁⲩ ('their, of-them') + ⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ (Lyc. plural of ⲉⲓⲱⲧ 'father') = 'their fathers,' subject of the two qualitative-perfects. ⲁⲩⲥⲱⲧ rendered as 'were drawn-out' (taking ⲥⲱⲧ from ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲥⲏⲧ root with sense of stretching/extension), pairing antithetically with ⲁⲩⲥⲃⲁⲕ 'were diminished.' The catechumen's question contrasts ancestral longevity with present brevity. Alternative: ⲛⲧⲁⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲧⲉ as a verb-phrase 'they have come-to-be / multiplied' — but the noun-reading fits the discourse-context better.

Translated as 'share' (i.e. half/portion/division). The lexeme is unattested in our corpus; possibly Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲗⲡ̄/ⲥⲗⲏⲡ 'share, allotment' (cf. Crum 330b). The cosmological sense fits: each of the five time-lords has one 'share' in heaven (his fellow above) and one 'share' that rules below (over humanity and cattle). Alternative readings considered: 'first/foremost' (ⲱⲁⲣⲡ with l-r alternation and prosthetic ⲥ-), 'appointed-one,' or 'herald' (Greek σάλπιγξ). Flagged for parallels.

Rendered 'they became (people) of (long) years' — taking ⲁⲩⲟⲛ as Lyc. perfect of ⲱⲛ 'be, become' or ⲱⲛϩ 'live,' with ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩ-ⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲉ as 'of years' (predicate). The phrase together with following ⲉⲩⲣⲍⲁⲍ ⲛⲁⲍⲉ 'being many in lifespan' describes the long-lived early generations.

Read as 'after him and after their cessation' — ⲙⲛⲛⲥⲱϩ 'after him' (3sg.m suffix) + ⲙⲛ̄- 'and' + ⲛⲥⲁ-ⲧⲟⲩ-ⲗⲟ 'after their ceasing.' ⲗⲟ = 'cease, stop' (qualitative). The phrase marks the temporal handover from year-lords to month-lords in the cosmological succession.

Translated 'lifespan' (= Sah. ⲱⲛϩ̄/ⲁϩⲉ). Confirmed by the parallel ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲍⲉ 'their lifespan' in line 31. The page consistently uses ⲁⲍⲉ for span-of-life: ⲣⲍⲁⲍ ⲛⲁⲍⲉ 'many in lifespan' (line 26), ⲡⲁⲍⲉ ⲛⲛⲉⲧⲁⲩⲭⲡⲁⲩ 'lifespan of those they begot' (line 32 restoration).

Translated as 'we have spent (our) years' (= 'we have aged'). The form is ⲁ-ⲛ-ⲣ̄- + ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ where ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ is the same lexeme that appears in ⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ/ⲣⲡ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ 'years' in this kephalaion (lines 11, 18, 19). This closes the previous chapter; the new chapter begins after the leer.

Identified as 'months,' Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉⲃⲟⲧ. The text establishes a hierarchical sequence of cosmic time-authorities: years (ⲣⲡ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ) → months (ⲃⲉⲧⲉ) → days (ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ) → hours (ⲛⲁⲩⲉ) → moments (ⲥⲟⲩⲥⲟⲩ). Each subsequent power's offspring lives a shorter lifetime. The hierarchy is decisive for the identification.
Translated 'way/manner' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲛⲟ 'manner'); contextually the parallel of ⲧⲍⲉ 'manner' in line 6 confirms a manner-particle.
Rendered 'their lifetime' from ⲁⲍⲉ = ⲁϩⲉ 'lifetime, age, period.' Recurs as ⲡⲁⲍⲉ in lines 5, 10 with same meaning.
Translated 'have diminished' on the model of ⲇⲱⲭⲃⲉ ('diminish/decrease') in accumulated vocabulary; the doubled-vowel ⲟ̄ⲱ may reflect perfect aspect or dialectal lengthening.

Read as ⲁ-ⲧⲁ-ⲡⲧⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'than the today/present (one),' completing the comparison between first generations (with abundant life and light) and the present age. ⲡⲧⲟⲟⲩⲉ as 'today/present' is tentative; the form spans into line 14 (-ⲟⲩⲉ).

Translated 'become long.' Probably from a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲓⲁⲩ/ⲟⲩⲏⲩ 'be far/long' — fits the context of the ancients' long lifespans contrasted with the short ones of the latter generation (ⲛⲓⲍⲁⲉⲩⲉ ⲥⲃⲁⲕ in line 20).
Translated 'diminishing/lessening,' a verbal noun on a root meaning decrease (cf. ⲗⲟⲓϫⲉ 'decrease'). The parallel ⲃⲓⲧϥ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('taken from the world') in line 22 confirms a sense of subtraction.
Read as ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ (Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ) = 'this saying / this matter.' Word division across line break: line 26 ends with ⲡⲓⲥⲉ, line 27 begins with ⲭⲉ; ⲡⲓⲥⲉϫⲉ is a coherent construction 'this word/saying.'

Read as ⲥⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲛϥ̄ 'recognize it' per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲥⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'recognize/discern.' Functions imperatively in the construction ⲁⲗⲗⲁ ⲥⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲛϥ̄ ⲁⲉ ⲛⲕⲙ̄ⲙⲉ ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'but recognize it that thou mayest understand it.'
Translated 'they are pure' from ⲟⲩⲱⲡⲉ/ⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ 'be pure, holy.' Splits across line 30/31 (ⲥⲉⲟⲩⲁ- / -ⲃⲉ).

ⲛⲉⲩⲉⲓⲣⲉ ⲡⲉ + temporal phrase = 'they were spending (a great chronos),' a periphrastic imperfect with the cognate-time accusative. The Greek loan ⲭⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'time-duration' fits the discussion of long ancient lifespans.

Lyc. ⲁⲧⲉ = Sah. ⲟⲟⲧⲉ 'womb.' The exclamation 'O what a multitude in one womb!' opens an enumeration: 5, then 7, then more or fewer at a time. The chapter contrasts the prolific many-in-one-womb births of the ancient men with the small, weak, single births of today.

The lexeme is ambiguous. Possibilities: (a) ⲛⲉⲩ-ϩⲁⲉ 'their last/posterity'; (b) ⲛⲉⲩ-ϩⲁⲓ 'their husbands'; (c) part of a compound 'ⲛⲉⲩ-ϩⲁ-ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ' = 'their multitude.' I have left a lacuna marker {2} and translated 'their {?}.' The verb ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ 'multiplied' is clear.
Possibly ⲉ-ⲡⲉⲓ-ⲁⲏ 'unto this end' (ⲁⲏ = Lyc. for ϩⲁⲏ 'last, end'). Translated 'this end' as terminus of the dwelling-on-the-earth phrase. Could alternatively be parsed differently.
Verbal compound ⲣ̄- + ⲟ̄ⲁⲭⲉ. Possibly Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲱϫⲉ/ⲟϣϫ 'be diminished, be deficient, fall short.' Context (parallel to ⲥⲁⲃⲕ 'small') confirms a verb of diminishment. Translated 'diminished.'

The same root ⲱⲭⲃⲉ recurs from line 3 (ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲭⲃⲉ 'they did not exceed/diminish'). In context 'two parts or X or more' a third quantity-marker is required. Could be a numeral ('three') or 'a lesser/diminished number.' Sense uncertain — translated as a placeholder via apparatus.

Difficult phrase. Tentative reading: ⲡⲕⲉⲟ 'the other (kind)' + ⲛ̄ⲟⲁⲓⲉ from ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲉ/ⲟⲩⲏ 'be far, distant, long-removed.' Translated 'become another (kind) at a remove' to capture the sense of the moderns being a different and lesser kind compared to the ancients.

ⲥⲃⲁⲩⲉ taken as plural of ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching' (in mandatory terminology). The shift from physical members to teachings/counsel is theologically apt: small in stature, weak in members, weak also in their teachings and counsel — degeneration on every level.

ⲡⲕⲉⲙⲟⲩ 'the other death' = the second death (eternal death) of standard Manichaean eschatology. ⲧⲉϩⲁⲩ likely qualitative of ϩⲁⲩ 'be bad/evil.' ⲛⲟ̄ⲗⲁⲙ tentatively 'of darkness' (cf. Sah. ⲱⲗⲙ̄ 'be defiled, dark') — the bad/evil-of-darkness is the eternal death. Could alternatively be Hebrew/Greek olam/aiōn 'eternity.' Translated 'is bad — of darkness.'
